raw_response:
I've been working this land for 45 years, and I know what our soil in Quzhou can give back. With 35 mu and just my wife and me at home, I have to be organized. I split the land: 25 mu on the wheat-maize rotation, and 10 mu for cotton on the lighter ground near the south end — that plot never drained well enough for good wheat anyway.

For my winter wheat on 25 mu, I'll sow Jimai 22 — the county extension station showed good trials last year and my neighbor Old Wang got 520 kg/mu with it. Base fertilizer I put down at plowing: about 40 kg of diammonium phosphate and 15 kg of potassium chloride per mu, then urea topdressing around returning-green stage, maybe 20 kg/mu. That gets me roughly 20 kg N, 8 kg P, 9 kg K per mu. I water four times with the well — before winter, returning-green, jointing, and grain-filling. Three sprays usually: one for aphids and powdery mildew, one for wheat midge, and a combined micronutrient spray at flowering. I plough every third year to break the hardpan; this year it's rotary tillage since I ploughed last autumn.

For summer maize following wheat, I go no-tillage direct seeding — saves time and the stubble holds moisture. Zhengdan 958 hybrid, same as always, reliable. 18 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu, most as compound fertilizer at sowing plus urea side-dressing at big-trumpet stage. Two irrigations, two sprays for borers and armyworm.

Cotton on 10 mu — I use Bt hybrid seed, that saves me many sprays. 16 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K per mu because cotton is a heavy potassium feeder and fiber quality depends on it. Three irrigations, four sprays mainly for aphids and mirid bugs since bollworm is handled by the Bt gene. Plough before planting — cotton needs deep loose soil.

Cost-wise I'll spend around 280 yuan/mu on wheat fertilizer, 220 on maize, 350 on cotton. Higher than strictly necessary on N maybe, but at my age I won't gamble on a thin harvest.
